hypothesis: Across ages within each sex, measured body weight scales approximately as the cube of measured stature, so the log-log slope of weight on stature is near 3 and most of the age-to-age shape of the weight curve is accounted for by cubing the stature curve.
pass_criterion: Using NHANES examined participants aged 2-19 y with measured standing height and weight, fit OLS log(weight kg) = a + b*log(height cm) separately by sex (survey-weighted). Claim supported if b lies in [2.6, 3.4] for both sexes AND, across single-year age medians, the cubed median-stature curve (scaled to match weight at age 2) explains R^2 >= 0.70 of the variance in median weight-for-age, with the remainder (the 'not wholly' part) being the minority.
fail_criterion: Claim refuted if b falls outside [2.4, 3.6] for either sex, or if the 95% CI for b excludes [2.6, 3.4] entirely for either sex, or if R^2 of median weight against scaled median stature cubed across ages is below 0.50.
interpretation: Thompson's 'linear dimension' is mapped to measured standing stature (recumbent length excluded) and 'weight' to measured body mass in kg. 'Tend to vary as the cube' is read as a log-log allometric exponent near 3 across the growth period; 'mainly though not wholly' allows departures from 3 due to changing body proportions and BMI rising with age. Modern reinterpretation: a cross-sectional age series in a national survey stands in for individual longitudinal growth, and the exponent is estimated by regression rather than by Thompson's visual curve comparison. Pooling several NHANES cycles is permitted.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES examination component records measured (not self-reported) standing height (BMXHT, cm) and weight (BMXWT, kg) in the Body Measures files, with age (RIDAGEYR), sex (RIAGENDR) and exam survey weights (WTMEC2YR) in the Demographics files, allowing direct estimation of the weight-stature exponent by sex and age.
